content.text: {"answers": [{"question_id": "Q1", "question": "What event or condition causes the organizer to start the room reservation process — for example, is it triggered by creating a calendar event, receiving a meeting request, or some other action?", "answer": "The organizer collects meeting date, time, and participant count, then begins the reservation process."}, {"question_id": "Q2", "question": "What system or method does the organizer currently use to check room availability — for instance, a shared calendar, a dedicated booking platform, or a physical sign-up sheet?", "answer": "The organizer uses a calendar system and a room reservation system to check availability."}, {"question_id": "Q3", "question": "If the preferred room is not available at the requested time, what steps does the organizer take — do they select an alternative room, propose a different time, or follow an escalation path?", "answer": "Room unavailability is listed as an exception; the specific fallback steps are not specified."}, {"question_id": "Q4", "question": "How are participants informed of the confirmed room details — is this done through an automatic calendar invitation, a manual email, a messaging tool, or another channel?", "answer": "The organizer creates a calendar invitation and notifies participants via email or a collaboration tool."}, {"question_id": "Q5", "question": "What is the process when a reserved meeting is cancelled or rescheduled — who is responsible for releasing the room, and how is that action carried out?", "answer": "Cancellation and rescheduling steps are not specified in the workflow."}, {"question_id": "Q6", "question": "Is any employee permitted to reserve a meeting room, or are there role-based restrictions or an approval step required before a reservation is confirmed?", "answer": "Role restrictions or approval steps are not specified; the meeting organizer reserves the room directly."}]}
